Yes. The matching paper by Tripti Shukla is HASTE: Hierarchical and Attribute-aware Supervision for Generative Recommendation [1]. It introduces hierarchical supervision for generative recommendation through a Hierarchical Loss that supervises each level of semantic IDs, plus attribute-specific losses that preserve fine-grained item attributes [1]. The paper says this improves training efficiency, accelerates convergence by about 2x versus standard causal cross-entropy, and improves long-tail recommendation performance across a fashion benchmark and multiple Amazon domains [1].

If you also mean related hierarchical supervision work beyond Shukla’s paper, several papers differ in focus: HoloRec uses hierarchical semantic encoding and supervised alignment for reasoning-oriented generation [2], HRPO turns item-level outcome feedback into dense token-aligned signals for post-training [4], and EchoRec uses multi-horizon auxiliary supervision for dense preference alignment rather than hierarchy over semantic ID levels [10].
